title: Number bonds
keyIdea: Number bonds within 20 are pairs of numbers that add to a total up to 20, plus the related subtraction fact. If 8 + 7 = 15, then 15 − 7 = 8. Quick recall of these bonds means you do not recount from one every time.
familyTip: Play 'I say 8 + 7' and wait for 15, then ask 'so 15 take away 7?'. Use two colours of counters for each part of the bond.

visual.caption: True bond idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

items: pairs and related facts up to 20

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build bonds to 15 and 18, use related subtraction, snap recall, catch make-10-only myth.

kid: A number bond is a pair that adds to a total. Within 20 you need many pairs, not only partners of 10.
If 8 + 7 = 15, then 15 − 7 = 8. The same bond helps subtraction.
Try to snap the answer quickly: hear 9 + 6 and say 15 without counting every bead.
Bonds within 20 are addition pairs and the matching take-away facts you can recall.
adult: NC Y1 addition and subtraction: recall number bonds (addition and related subtraction facts) within 20. Distinct from bonds to 10 on a ten-frame (K.OA.4 / 'Number bonds to 9' topic).
Words: number bond, pair, related fact, within 20, recall. Common mistakes: treating bonds as only make-10; recounting every subtraction from 1; off-by-one sums (8+7 as 14 or 17).
In the lab your child builds 8+7 and 11+7, uses 15−7=8, snaps 9+6, and spots the make-10-only mix-up.
